purpose: Conditional diagnostic goal injection after the main automatic pipeline misses its predeclared scope; isolate goal discovery from test implementation.
interpretation: A diagnostic success is manual-goal-conditioned test-generation evidence, never automatic target discovery. Preserve main failures and diagnostic cost separately.
source_policy: Original public issue and existing original test spans support every goal. No generated candidate, native failure or posterior implementation root cause supplies the goal.

goal.existing_validation: The original streaming NDJSON host checks values before EOF and closure after normal exhaustion. Another original test checks malformed NDJSON using memory content. These checks do not combine an active stream with a parse error before EOF.
goal.missing_relation: When JSON iteration starts on a legal streaming response and then terminates because a record is malformed, the same Response must close. The original tests do not observe this failure path.
goal.preconditions: Use the original host streaming-content boundary, an allowed NDJSON content type, and a valid codec. Include a complete malformed record before an additional unread chunk so ordinary EOF cleanup cannot supply the observation. Existing imports must suffice.
goal.object_binding: The iterator, parsing exception and post-error closure observation refer to the same Response and underlying stream.
goal.operations: Create the streaming response. Iterate until the malformed record raises. Observe closure after that exception and before any explicit cleanup or unrelated consumption.
goal.observation: Observe the required DecodingError and response.is_closed immediately after the parser terminates by error.
goal.expectation: Malformed NDJSON raises DecodingError. Once JSON streaming iteration has begun, its termination must close that Response, including termination by a parsing error. Do not impose a value on is_stream_consumed before or after a yield, an exact read count, or cancellation behavior.
goal.oracle_basis: Original public issue lines 1, 8 and 12 require incremental NDJSON parsing, per-line validity, and streaming iteration consumption and closure. Original tests at 850 and 860 distinguish malformed memory input from normal streaming closure; tests at 926 enforce normal streaming closure.

reference_source_receipts.role: Malformed memory payload and normal incremental stream are separate checks.
Normal exhaustion closes streaming responses in sync and async tests.

goals.input_binding_only: seed_alias and evidence_ids currently use strict-main identities. A later diagnostic runner may replace only these IDs by exact original test/source identity in its separately frozen protocol; no fuzzy matching or content changes.
exclusions: No hidden evaluator or reference patch

goal.existing_validation: The original bulk safe-mode host successfully updates one row and checks its value. The separate non-aggregate invariant test rejects inserts that violate a registered per-row predicate. The bulk UPDATE host does not register an invariant.
goal.missing_relation: A bulk UPDATE under safe mode can change a field governed by a registered invariant. Validation must reject the resulting invalid state and restore the previous row, even when the SQL UPDATE itself is legal.
goal.preconditions: Use one existing row in the original file-backed database. Register a persistent non-aggregate invariant on the field that the UPDATE will change. The original row must satisfy it; the updated value must violate it. Use existing API helpers and imports. Keep the SQL UPDATE otherwise valid.
goal.object_binding: Invariant registration, the bulk CLI database path, the UPDATE target table, and the post-operation read must refer to the same database and table.
goal.operations: Create a valid single-row state. Enable safe import and register the field predicate. Invoke bulk with the original UPDATE shape, --nl and --safe-mode using one record that violates that predicate. Reopen or query the same database after the command.
goal.observation: Observe a non-zero CLI exit and exact restoration of the original row. A single row or explicit key/order avoids unspecified multi-row ordering.
goal.expectation: The registered predicate must be checked after writes. Its failure prevents commit and restores the pre-operation row. An SQL constraint failure alone does not establish this invariant-validation interaction. Do not require opaque invariant IDs to be truthy or assume a particular ID format.
goal.oracle_basis: Original public issue lines 1, 12–18 and 29–34 require persistent per-row invariants, validation after safe writes, exact rollback on failure, bulk UPDATE support, and a non-zero exit when the safe operation does not commit.

reference_source_receipts.role: Safe mode validates invariants after writes and rolls back all safe-mode failures.
Registered invariant API and row-wise/nonaggregate predicate semantics.
Bulk safe mode supports UPDATE and exits zero only on commit.
Existing nonaggregate invariant failure check uses safe_bulk_insert.
Existing bulk UPDATE checks a successful update without registered invariant.
